solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: One caught in face, the whole thing seen in theatre (5,4)

indicators.note: IC is caught inside the face, held within its letters

blocks.note: c = caught, the cricket scorecard abbreviation

annotation.surface: Someone takes one in the face while watching a whole show at the theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a punch taken at a show, but 'One caught' is two abbreviations, not a person hit. A music hall is a British variety theatre of the Victorian and Edwardian era.
annotation.definitionFit: A music hall is a theatre staging variety acts.

entries.clue: Significant ruin besetting Scots sweetheart (5)

indicators.note: to beset is to surround, so MAR surrounds JO

blocks.note: jo is Scots for a sweetheart, as in Burns's 'John Anderson, my jo'

annotation.surface: A significant disaster threatens a Scottish lover.
annotation.walkthrough: JO is a Scots word for a sweetheart, familiar from Burns and a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a major change is a significant one, the adjective used of importance rather than rank.

entries.clue: Thought experiment good in chain store with CD-Rs distributed (12,3)

indicators.note: the letters are dealt out afresh in a new order

annotation.surface: A shop in a chain handing out recordable CDs.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all retail, with good and CD-Rs sounding like stock, but every letter of it is fodder. The answer is Schrodinger's famous quantum thought experiment, with a cat both alive and dead.
annotation.definitionFit: Schrodinger's cat is the thought experiment in which a boxed cat is both alive and dead until observed.

entries.clue: Incautious having wine and pork pie before run (8)

indicators.note: puts R after the other pieces

blocks.note: pork pie is rhyming slang for a lie (porky)

annotation.surface: A careless person enjoys wine and a pork pie before going for a run.
annotation.walkthrough: Pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang: pork pie rhymes with lie, and a 'porky' is a fib. The surface's picnic food is really a falsehood.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym by attitude: the swaggering Royalist cavaliers gave their name to a careless, offhand disregard for risk.

entries.clue: Commander horrified — good man lost (4)

indicators.note: something lost is no longer there, so the good man goes missing from the word for horrified

blocks.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST; removed from AGHAST

annotation.surface: A commander is appalled at the loss of a fine man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good man' for ST (saint) is a standard crossword convention. An agha is a commander or chief in the Ottoman Empire.
annotation.definitionFit: An agha was an Ottoman military commander or chief officer.

entries.clue: Police Muswell Hill area: rising crime brings court action (4,6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising turns the word upwards, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: Muswell Hill in north London has the postcode N10, read as N TEN

annotation.surface: Muswell Hill police notice a rise in local crime that leads to prosecutions.
annotation.walkthrough: Muswell Hill is a north London district whose postcode is N10, spelt out here as N TEN. 'Court action' looks legal after all that policing, but the court is a tennis court.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example with a pun: a court case is legal action, but the sport played on a grass court is action of another kind.

entries.clue: Animal taking look outside for snare (5)

indicators.note: to take something is to take it in, so the look holds the animal
places the look on the outside, one letter either side of the animal

annotation.surface: A trapper checks a snare to see whether an animal has been caught.
annotation.walkthrough: LO as an old exclamation meaning look is a crossword staple.
annotation.definitionFit: A lasso is a rope loop for catching, or snaring, animals.

entries.clue: Around over time, cat’s getting cream (6)

indicators.note: the cat's letters go around OT

blocks.note: a lion is a big cat; cat's = cat is, placed around OT

annotation.surface: Over time, a cat is fed cream.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cat's getting cream' is a cosy picture of a pet with a saucer, but the cream is a skin lotion and the cat a lion.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: cream here is the cosmetic or medicinal kind you rub on skin, not dairy.

entries.clue: Volunteer officer with Labour offering faster service (7,8)

blocks.note: a special constable is a volunteer police officer in Britain, called a special

annotation.surface: A volunteer teams up with the Labour Party promising quicker public services.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a special constable, or special, is an unpaid volunteer police officer. Capitalised Labour suggests the political party, but it is the labour of childbirth.
annotation.definitionFit: Special delivery is the postal service that gets items there faster.

entries.clue: BEF endlessly destroy supply ships — in Pearl Harbour? (6-3)

indicators.note: BEF loses its last letter
the letters are shipped about supply, that is flexibly, into a new order

annotation.surface: A war report: the British Expeditionary Force sets out to sink enemy supply ships, perhaps at Pearl Harbor.
annotation.walkthrough: The BEF was the British Expeditionary Force of both world wars, and Pearl Harbor steers the solver to war at sea. The definition is cryptic: an oyster bed is where pearls are harboured.
annotation.definitionFit: An oyster bed harbours the oysters that grow pearls, so it is a pearl harbour.

entries.clue: St John’s view as he converted sectarian (8,7)

indicators.note: the letters are converted into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A saint's opinion as he became a member of a sect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Converted' fits a religious surface so well that it hardly reads as an instruction, and the answer is a religious convert too.
annotation.definitionFit: A Jehovah's Witness belongs to a religious sect, so is a sectarian.

entries.clue: Turning to large caviare sandwiches for grub (6)

indicators.note: something turning faces the other way, so the little word reads backwards
ROE holds OT and L between its slices

blocks.note: used as printed, then turned round
l = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: Someone turns to large caviar sandwiches for food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like a noun for food after the sandwiches, but it is the verb: to grub about, to rootle.
annotation.definitionFit: To rootle is to grub or rummage about, as a pig does with its snout.

entries.clue: Poison a drink back at home with MDMA (8)

indicators.note: PORT is written back to front

blocks.note: port is a fortified wine; reversed to TROP
MDMA is the drug ecstasy, E

annotation.surface: Someone is poisoned by a drink spiked at home with ecstasy.
annotation.walkthrough: MDMA is ecstasy, which crosswords abbreviate to E.
annotation.definitionFit: Atropine is a poisonous alkaloid found in deadly nightshade.

entries.clue: Fish with line and instrument for deep sound (6,4)

indicators.note: sets the fish beside the line; the line comes first

annotation.surface: An angler with a line, and a sonar device for the deep.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deep sound' suggests a stretch of sea (a sound) and fishing gear, but it is low-pitched music. The pieces are taken in the order of the answer, line before fish.
annotation.definitionFit: The string bass, or double bass, is the deepest-sounding bowed string instrument.

entries.clue: Rock one to settle in European river (10)

indicators.note: the one settling goes in the river, as a stone sinks into water

blocks.note: the Rhone flows through Switzerland and France

annotation.surface: A stone sinks and settles in a European river.
annotation.walkthrough: With the answer's first letters in, the Rhine looks like the European river, but it leaves STONE to explain; the river that fits is split round the insert. 'Rock' is slang for a gem.
annotation.definitionFit: A rock is slang for a gem, and a rhinestone is a paste gem.

entries.clue: Island insurance recalled as subject to cancellation? (9)

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so ELBA COVER is read back to front

annotation.surface: An island's insurance policy is withdrawn because it could be cancelled.
annotation.walkthrough: The indicator 'recalled' also suggests cancellation, so the surface sounds like revocation twice over. The question mark admits that 'subject to cancellation' is a loose gloss.
annotation.definitionFit: What is revocable can be revoked, that is cancelled.

entries.clue: Sing Bachelor Boy when daughter’s born (4)

indicators.note: the D of daughter is replaced by the B of born

blocks.note: b = born, as in genealogies; it takes D's place

annotation.surface: Someone sings Cliff Richard's song Bachelor Boy when a baby girl arrives.
annotation.walkthrough: Bachelor Boy was a 1962 Cliff Richard hit, which makes 'Sing' look musical. Here it means to sing to the police: to inform, or blab.
annotation.definitionFit: To sing is slang for informing, spilling secrets, which is to blab.

entries.clue: Meringue ingredient for example affected weight (3,5)

indicators.note: WEIGHT is affected, its letters disturbed

annotation.surface: A recipe note: a meringue ingredient, for instance, alters the weight.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like baking advice, which hides that 'affected' is working on weight.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: meringue is whisked from the whites of eggs with sugar.

entries.clue: Star not quite convert to compassionate eating? (4)

indicators.note: something not quite finished stops short, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: someone who has taken up eating that spares animals; the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A celebrity who has not quite gone vegan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Star' reads as a celebrity dabbling in veganism, but it is the bright star in Lyra.
annotation.definitionFit: Vega is one of the brightest stars in the night sky.

entries.clue: 2’s paradoxical states exhibited in zombies? (6,4)

annotation.definitionNote: the first definition is two adjectives describing states, not a noun

blocks.note: Schrodinger's cat, the answer to 2 down, is at once living and dead
zombies are corpses that walk, dead yet moving; the question mark flags the loose fit

annotation.surface: The cat's paradox, alive and dead at once, is shown by zombies.
annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 2 down, SCHRODINGER'S CAT, which is both living and dead until the box is opened. Zombies are the other way to be both.
annotation.definitionFit: Zombies are called the living dead, and Schrodinger's cat is in a living and dead state.

entries.clue: Beater at Murthly finally getting dram (6)

indicators.note: takes the final letter of Murthly

annotation.surface: A beater on a Scottish grouse shoot at Murthly gets a dram at the end of the day.
annotation.walkthrough: Murthly is a village in Perthshire with a shooting estate, and a beater drives game towards the guns. The beater here is a kitchen whisk.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by the usual contents: a dram is a small Scottish measure of spirits, nearly always of this one.

entries.clue: Hard cutting cost of transport in Hannibal’s birthplace (8)

indicators.note: H cuts into CARTAGE, splitting it

blocks.note: cartage is the charge for carrying goods

annotation.surface: Tough cuts to the cost of transport in the city where Hannibal was born.
annotation.walkthrough: Hannibal, the general who crossed the Alps with elephants, suits a transport surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Hannibal was born in Carthage, in present-day Tunisia.

entries.clue: Stupid or wise as Member of Parliament? (6)

blocks.note: the bird is a symbol of wisdom, yet its solemn stare can also look dim
a parliament is the collective noun for a group of owls, so 'as' a member means like that bird

annotation.surface: A jibe at MPs: are they fools or sages?
annotation.walkthrough: Member of Parliament reads as an MP, but a parliament is the collective noun for owls.
annotation.definitionFit: Owlish describes a solemn look that can seem wise or merely stupid.

entries.clue: Be unable to stand, necking last of Chablis in hurry (5)

indicators.note: HATE swallows the S, as if downing a drink
takes the final letter of Chablis

annotation.surface: Someone downs the rest of the Chablis in a rush and can no longer stand up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Be unable to stand' suggests being drunk, and 'necking' suggests drinking; both are misdirection, meaning to hate and to swallow.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: to do something in haste is to do it in a hurry.

entries.clue: Middleman oddly ignored hypothesis (4)

indicators.note: the odd letters are ignored, keeping the even ones

annotation.surface: A go-between's theory was brushed aside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oddly ignored' keeps the even letters, which is easy to get backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A hypothesis is an idea put forward for testing.

entries.clue: Rolling cask into best clubs, do they bother in saloons? (8,7)

indicators.note: the cask rolls, tumbling its letters
the rolled cask is put into the word for best, like a barrel rolled into a cellar

annotation.surface: Pub landlords rolling a cask while others ask whether they bother in saloon bars.
annotation.walkthrough: Casks and saloons make a pub, but a saloon is also a British name for a sedan car. 'Best' looks like an adjective and is the verb, to beat.
annotation.definitionFit: Backseat drivers pester the driver of a car such as a saloon.

entries.clue: Guard leaving southern gate (5)

indicators.note: a guard leaving deserts his post, so the southern letter departs from the guard's word

annotation.surface: A guard deserts his post at the southern gate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Southern gate' reads as a place, but southern only supplies the S that the guard loses.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym by function: a gate is a way in, the place you enter by.

entries.clue: Don’t do away with Phoenician city corporation (5,4)

indicators.note: joins the two pieces in order

blocks.note: to spare is not to kill off
Tyre, the ancient Phoenician port in Lebanon

annotation.surface: A plea not to demolish an ancient city's corporation.
annotation.walkthrough: A corporation here is the old jokey word for a pot belly, and a spare tyre is a roll of fat round the waist.
annotation.definitionFit: Corporation and spare tyre are both jocular words for a paunch.
